about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2024 only.

rows.name: Table of contents
rows.printed_heading: TABLE OF CONTENTS
rows.what_it_is: The report's index. Unlike FY2023 it gives page RANGES ('Pages 23-26') rather than a single start page, and its financial-schedule names are the names the accountant's software produces.
rows.columns: (section/report name) | Page(s) n
rows.layout: two pages, name left, 'Page n' or 'Pages n-m' right
rows.notes: This is the definitive list of what the FY2024 financial section contains, and it contains NO revenue/receipts schedule and NO general fund appropriations schedule — see the 'surprises'. Entries under Accountant: 'Balance Sheet for FY Ending June 30, 2024 Page 21', 'General Fund Accounts Receivable Detail Page 22', 'Special Revenue Fund Balance Detail Pages 23-26', 'Capital Project Fund Page 27', 'Combining Balance Sheet- Enterprise Funds Page 28', 'Trust Fund Balance Detail Page 29', 'Undesignated Fund Balance Roll-forward Page 30'. Under Treasurer/Collector: 'Treasurer's Cash as of June 30, 2024 Page 33', 'Trust Funds Page 34', 'Trust and Stabilization Funds Held by Other Banks Page 35', 'Five Years Outstanding Debt Page 36', 'Debt Repayment Schedule Page 37', 'Collection of Taxes Receivables Summary Pages 38-39'. Note it also gives a section FY2023 did not have: 'State & National Election Results 175-184'. 'Elected Officials: Sate and Local' is a typo on the page.

rows.name: Town profile fact block
rows.printed_heading: LUNENBURG PROFILE
rows.what_it_is: Single-value town facts above a narrative description, same form as FY2023.
rows.columns: (label)- (value)
rows.layout: centred list of LABEL-VALUE lines
rows.notes: FY'24 TAX RATE- $14.10 (down from $14.62 in FY23); REGISTERED VOTERS- 9,468 (up from 9,041). Same eight fields as FY2023 — this is the only place in either report where the tax rate appears as a figure.

rows.name: Elected officials roster (state and local)
rows.printed_heading: ELECTED OFFICIALS
rows.what_it_is: Elected officeholders with term expiry years; page 7 is state/federal with addresses and phones, 8-9 are town boards.
rows.columns: (office / board, with member count and term length) | (name)-(term expiry year)
rows.layout: two-up columns of office headings each followed by names
rows.notes: Same run-together defect as FY2023: 'John T. RabbittSarah Cammer-- 20272026' (p8), 'Glenn McLeodMatt Allison--2025 2029' (p9). Board composition changed substantially from FY2023 — the whole Board of Assessors turned over.

rows.name: Appointed officials roster
rows.printed_heading: APPOINTED OFFICIALS
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed board, commission and staff post with members and term expiry years, including resignation dates.
rows.columns: (body or post, with member count and term) | (name)-(term expiry year)
rows.layout: six pages of headings and name lists, sometimes continued across a page break ('ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE (continued)')
rows.notes: Cleaner text layer than FY2023 (all 'plain' extraction, no OCR). Annotations inline: 'Matthew Allison- Resigned 6/3 2024'. NOTE a probable duplication: the heading 'INSPECTOR OF PLUMBING/GAS / Gary Williams' appears at the top of BOTH page 13 and page 15. New bodies appear that FY2023 did not list, including an Economic Development Committee and a Personnel Committee.

rows.name: Enterprise funds combining balance sheet (printed twice)
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Combining Balance Sheet - Enterprise Funds / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: Assets, liabilities and fund equity of the four enterprise funds (Sewer, Water, Trash/Solid Waste, PEG Access) side by side with a memorandum-only total column.
rows.columns: Sewer Enterprise Fund | Water Enterprise Fund | Enterprise Fund | Enterprise Fund | Enterprise Fund | (three empty fund columns) | (Memorandum Only) total
rows.layout: one wide table filling the page, nine money columns, with a PROOF row of zeros at the foot
rows.printed_total: Total Liabilities and Fund Equity 5,573,383.92 | 65,079.88 | 214,850.51 | 1,032,714.29 | 0.00 x4 | 6,886,028.60; Total Assets identical; PROOF 0.00 across
rows.notes: PAGES 21 AND 28 ARE THE SAME TABLE WITH THE SAME NUMBERS. The table of contents says page 21 should be 'Balance Sheet for FY Ending June 30, 2024' — i.e. the town-wide combined balance sheet that FY2023 printed on its page 24. That town-wide balance sheet is NOT IN THIS REPORT; the enterprise-funds sheet was printed in its place. Page 21's copy also lost the fund-name column headers, which page 28 has. OCR reads some zeros as letters ('0.0U', 'U.UU', 'U.OU').

rows.name: General fund accounts receivable detail
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / General Fund Accounts Receivable Detail / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: The general fund's non-tax receivables by MUNIS account number, showing how much was received in the first quarter of the following year and what is still outstanding.
rows.columns: Account Number | Account Name | Accounts Receivable | Deferred Revenue | Receipts thru 9/30/2024 | Remaining Receivable 6/30/2024
rows.layout: clean six-column table with about 24 blank rows below the data (an unfilled template)
rows.printed_total: otal General Fund Accounts Receivable Detail [sic, leading T lost] 1,275,638.93 | 1,275,638.93 | 0.00 | 0.00
rows.notes: Only seven rows carry data and three of them lost their Account Name in OCR. The account numbers are MUNIS org-object codes (0100-134100 etc.), which is the first time this format appears in an annual report. Largest row: Coastal Rescue Wagon Receivable 386,510.09. This is a receivables schedule, not a revenue schedule — do not read it as receipts.

rows.name: Special revenue fund balance detail
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Special Revenue Fund Balance Detail / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: Every special revenue fund by MUNIS fund number with its closing fund balance, plus receipts in the following quarter and any remaining deficit. This is the FY2024 successor to FY2023's Special Revenue Funds schedule, but it reports a BALANCE only — the year's receipts and disbursements columns are gone.
rows.columns: Fund Number | Fund Name | Accounts Receivable | Deferred Revenue | Fund Balance 6/30/2024 | Receipts thru 9/30/2024 | BAN's | Remaining Deficit 6/30/2024
rows.layout: four consecutive pages, heading and column headers repeated; fund number left, name, then six money columns
rows.printed_total: Total Special Revenue Fund Balance 83.86 | 83.86 | $ 4,963,068.15 | 116,241.96 | 0.00 | (deficit column OCRs as 'S 171986-817')
rows.notes: IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM FY2023: FY2023's version (pages 34-43) gave forward balance, receipts, disbursements and closing balance for each fund. This one gives only the closing balance, so the year's flows through grants and revolving funds cannot be read from the FY2024 report at all. Fund names are UPPERCASE MUNIS descriptions ('REC LOST BOOKS', 'EXTENDED DAY REVOLVING', 'DRUG FORFEITURE - STATE'). Negative balances in parentheses (POLICE/FIRE DETAILS ($30,728.40), CUSTODIAN DETAILS ($9,326.34), HIGHWAY INSURANCE REC (5,126.68)). OCR sprays 'un us es es es' where a column of dollar signs was. One row's fund number is a range: '2577/2578/2579/: BOH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS'.

rows.name: Capital project fund balance detail
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Capital Project Fund Balance Detail / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: Each open capital project fund by MUNIS fund number with its closing balance, following-quarter receipts, and outstanding bond anticipation notes.
rows.columns: Fund Number | Fund Name | Enterprise Fund Name (if applicable) | Accounts Receivable | Deferred Revenue | Fund Balance 6/30/2024 | Receipts thru 9/30/2024 | BAN's 6/30/2024 | BAN's / Debt Issued 7/1/2024 - 9/30/2024 | Remaining Deficit 6/30/2024
rows.layout: one page, ten columns, about eight blank template rows at the foot
rows.printed_total: Total Capital Projects Fund Balance 0.00 | 0.00 | 3,575,303.03 | 0.00 | 152,499.00 | 0.00
rows.notes: MUCH less detailed than FY2023's capital schedule (page 44), which listed every individual project under its town-meeting article with authorised, spent and remaining amounts. Here whole capital plans are single rows ('FY23 CAPITAL PLAN 1,292,273.56', 'FY24 CAPITAL PLAN 1,011,043.00'), so project-level detail is not recoverable from the FY2024 report. OCR mangles several fund names ('FYZO CAPHIALPLAN', 'rYZI CAPIIAL PLAN', 'ACOUSTION OF STRFFTLGHTS', '30 SCHOOLS DEMOLION/DESIGN'). Two rows have negative balances offset by BANs (FY19 CAPITAL PLAN (96,099.00); PURCHASE SALIBA PROPERTY (56,400.00)).

rows.name: Trust fund balance detail
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Trust Fund Balance Detail / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: Every named trust, scholarship, stabilization and expendable trust fund with its closing balance.
rows.grain: one trust fund (non-expendable principal rows first, then a parallel set of '- Expendable' income rows)
rows.columns: Fund Number | Fund Name | Accounts Receivable | Deferred Revenue | Fund Balance 6/30/2024 | Receipts thru 9/30/2024 | BAN'S | Remaining Deficit 6/30/2024
rows.layout: one dense page of ~62 rows
rows.printed_total: Total Expendable Trust Fund Balance 0.00 | 0.00 | 9,034,631.47 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 (a sub-figure of $2,254,933.99 also prints on the line above)
rows.notes: Most of the Fund Balance column is blank in the OCR even though the rows exist — only the first ~20 rows carry visible amounts, so the schedule is largely unreadable as text despite being cleanly laid out. Names identify each donor bequest (Charles Dickerson Library, Dora Haven Cowdrey Scholarship, Chester Mossman Teen Center, American Legion Worthy Poor, J & M Howard Sidewalks/Grounds). Fund numbers repeat across rows (all Library trusts are 8114), so number alone does not identify a row.

rows.name: Undesignated fund balance roll-forward (free cash derivation)
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Undesignated Fund Balance Roll-forward / as of June 30, 2024 / (Unaudited)
rows.what_it_is: How the general fund's undesignated balance moved over the year: opening balance, prior-year reserves released, current-year reserves set aside, and the year's total revenue and expenditure closeouts.
rows.columns: (step label) | (amount)
rows.layout: single-column labelled list with amounts on the right, Add:/Less:/Deduct: section markers
rows.printed_total: Current Year Undesignated Fund Balance 2,751,841.80, with a PROOF UNDESIGNATED FUND BALANCE AGREES TO THE BALANCE SHEET line reading 0.00
rows.notes: THE MOST BUDGET-RELEVANT PAGE IN THE FY2024 REPORT. It is the only place FY2024 states a town-wide revenue and expenditure figure: 'Current Year Revenue Closeouts 47,116,149.83' and 'Current Year Expenditure Closeouts 46,463,708.05'. Beginning Undesignated Fund Balance 2,529,335.50; Prior Year Total Fund Balance 4,123,029.49 — both tie to FY2023's balance sheet. Current Year Reserved for Encumbrances 369,841.91 and for Expenditures 1,653,783.36. Many template rows are printed with no label and no value.

rows.name: Treasurer's cash by bank account
rows.printed_heading: TREASURER & TAX COLLECTOR / TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Treasurer's Cash as of 6/30/2024
rows.what_it_is: Every bank and investment account with its closing balance.
rows.columns: Bank Institution | Ending Balance
rows.layout: single two-column list
rows.printed_total: Total Treasurer Cash as of 06/30/2024  $ 28,904,434.36
rows.notes: Cleaner than FY2023's version and it now carries actual column headers ('Bank Institution' / 'Ending Balance'). Directly comparable to FY2023 page 48 ($27,244,162.79). Two accounts are new this year: 'Bartholomew Opioid Settlement Stabilization' ($176,302.50) and 'Fidelity Bank General Fund' ($100.00); the ARPA account moved from Unibank to Main Street Bank. One stray OCR artefact in the dollar column ('tA tA tA 92,636.63').

rows.name: Trust funds fiscal year summary (Bartholomew)
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / TRUST FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR 2024 SUMMARY (footer reads 'Page 2 of 2')
rows.what_it_is: Fund-by-fund activity for the trusts and stabilization funds held at Bartholomew & Company: beginning principal, earnings, transfers, expenditures, ending cash value, unrealized gain/loss, ending market value.
rows.grain: one trust or stabilization fund (with subtotal and grand total columns)
rows.columns: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | NET EARNINGS | TRANSFERS OF PRINCIPAL | EARNINGS TRANSFERS | EXPENDITURES | ENDING CASH VALUE | UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | CHANGE IN UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | ENDING MARKET VALUE
rows.layout: rotated landscape spreadsheet; OCR returned one line per COLUMN so rows are unrecoverable
rows.printed_total: 'GRAND TOTALS' column exists; values cannot be tied to rows in this OCR (the largest figures on the page are $6,015,341.47 and $5,886,028.59)
rows.notes: The footer says 'Page 2 of 2' — PAGE 1 OF THIS TWO-PAGE SCHEDULE IS NOT IN THE REPORT. (FY2023 had the same problem in a different shape: it printed pages 2, 3 and 4 of a nine-page schedule.) Fund families identifiable: GENERAL FUNDS, STABILIZATION FUNDS, MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS, PEG ACCESS ENTERPRISE FUND, plus named scholarships. Heading of column block reads 'ACCOUNTING METHOD: BOOK VALUE'.

rows.name: Trust and stabilization funds held by other banks
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / TRUST AND STABILIZATION FUNDS HELD BY OTHER BANKS / FISCAL YEAR 2022 SUMMARY [sic]
rows.what_it_is: The ten trust and stabilization funds NOT held at Bartholomew — MMDT, Unitil stock, Edward Jones, TD Banknorth, Unibank, Main Street Bank — with the year's principal, earnings, transfers, expenditures and ending values.
rows.columns: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | FY2024 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | FY2024 NET EARNINGS | FY2024 TRANSFERS OF PRINCIPAL | FY2024 EXPENDITURES | FY2024 ENDING CASH VALUE | FY2024 UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | FY2024 CHANGE IN UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | FY2024 ENDING MARKET VALUE
rows.layout: one clean upright table of ten rows plus a grand total; footer 'Page 1 of 1'
rows.notes: THE HEADING CONTRADICTS THE COLUMNS: it says 'FISCAL YEAR 2022 SUMMARY' while every column is labelled FY2024 and the figures are FY2024. A stale template label. Vehicle/Equipment Stabilization at Main Street Bank is the largest fund ($2,254,933.99 ending, $250,000.00 transferred in).

rows.name: Five years of outstanding debt
rows.printed_heading: FIVE YEARS OUTSTANDING DEBT / As of June 30, 2024
rows.what_it_is: Long-term debt by purpose for five years, inside and outside the general debt limit, plus short-term notes; then a list of authorised-but-unissued debt.
rows.grain: one debt purpose (row) x one year (column)
rows.layout: one clean five-year table, then an 'Authorized Unissued Debt and Prospective Financing' block with Amount / Purpose columns
rows.printed_total: Total Long-Term Indebtedness $33,256,561 (2024); Total Outstanding Indebtedness 33,409,060 (2024), then 35,868,300 / 39,206,582 / 42,495,303 / 46,372,354
rows.notes: Rolls forward FY2023's identical table by one year and every overlapping cell agrees exactly, so the two reports together give seven years 2018-2024. The Authorized Unissued Debt block again prints eight purposes with NO amounts (same eight as FY2023). Same footnote about excluding leases, overlapping debt and unfunded pension liability.

rows.name: Debt repayment schedule
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2024
rows.what_it_is: Future principal, interest and admin fee by fiscal year for every outstanding issue, with grand totals.
rows.grain: one fiscal year x one bond issue
rows.columns: FISCAL YEAR | (per-issue PRINCIPAL / INTEREST / ADMIN FEE / TOTAL blocks for each of ~10 issues) | GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL | GRAND TOTAL INTEREST
rows.layout: rotated landscape spreadsheet, ~30 columns; OCR returned 31 scrambled lines
rows.printed_total: grand total columns exist but no value is separable
rows.notes: Unreadable as text, like FY2023's equivalent. Issue identifiers that survive give the issue dates: 11/3/2005 SERIES 9 WATER, SERIES 13 MWPAT/MWCT 3/15/2007, 1/21/2015 SCH PROT BOND, 2/9/2016, 2/21/2018 SERIES 19 REFUNDING. Needs geometry-aware extraction.

rows.name: Receivables and collection of taxes summary
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES / RECEIVABLES SUMMARY / JUNE 30, 2024
rows.what_it_is: For each tax levy year and each receivable type: opening balance, commitments, abatements, payments, refunds, transfers, adjustments and closing balance. Real estate levies back to 2007, personal property back to 1998.
rows.grain: one levy year within one receivable type
rows.columns: FISCAL YEAR | FORWARD | COMMITIMENTS [sic] | ABATEMENTS | PAYMENTS | REFUNDS | TRANSFER | ADJUSTMENTS | BALANCES
rows.layout: two upright pages, row label left, eight money columns; grouped by receivable type (REAL ESTATE, PERSONAL PROPERTY, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE, betterments, sewer commitments)
rows.notes: DRAMATICALLY BETTER than FY2023's version of the same schedule: FY2023 printed it rotated across three pages and OCR destroyed it; here it is upright, two pages, and rows and columns line up. The single most useful figure for a levy question is on page 38: 'LEVY OF 2024 ... COMMITMENTS 30,853,785.94' with payments of (30,121,143.11) and a closing balance of 475,974.40. The heading 'FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES' is printed on both pages under a JUNE 30, 2024 date line — the identical stale label appears in FY2023's copy of this schedule, confirming it is the form's own text and not an OCR error.

rows.name: Cemetery interments for the year
rows.printed_heading: CEMETERY DIVISION - 2024
rows.what_it_is: Every person interred in a Lunenburg cemetery in 2024, by month, with age and which cemetery.
rows.columns: NAME | AGE | CEMETERY | (repeated as a second set of columns for the second half of the year)
rows.layout: two side-by-side blocks (Jan-Jul left, Aug-Dec right), each grouped under a month heading
rows.printed_total: a count is introduced by the partially-OCR'd line 'LEnt of people interred this year.' — the number itself did not survive
rows.notes: FY2023 HAS NO EQUIVALENT — this table exists only in FY2024. An asterisk before a name appears to mark veterans (some carry a service note underneath: '(Vietnam)', '(PeaceTime)'). Some rows lost their AGE. Cemeteries recorded as North, South, and one lot reference 'N/W East #28'.

rows.name: Senior property tax work-off program
rows.printed_heading: SENIOR PROPERTY TAX WORK-OFF PROGRAM / JANUARY 1, 2024 – NOVEMBER 1, 2024
rows.what_it_is: The rules and the year's participation in the programme that lets income-eligible seniors work off part of their property tax bill.
rows.grain: one eligibility rule / one participating department
rows.columns: (bulleted rules and department list)
rows.layout: narrative with two bulleted lists
rows.printed_total: nine residents, 640.50 hours, $9,607.50 in real estate tax abatements
rows.notes: FY2023 HAS NO EQUIVALENT SECTION. Carries the parameters as figures: 2024 abatement maximum $1,500 applied to the third-quarter bill, $15.00/hour, age 60+, income limits $50,000 one-person / $75,000 two-person. Six departments used the labour.

rows.name: Nashoba Associated Boards of Health service counts
rows.printed_heading: (none — counts printed under narrative sub-headings; the section banner is 'BOARD OF HEALTH' on p72)
rows.what_it_is: Activity counts for the shared health district: inspections, permits, Title 5 work, immunisations and home health visits.
rows.columns: (activity name) | (count)
rows.layout: a count printed at the right margin on the sub-heading line, with explanatory prose underneath
rows.notes: Directly comparable to FY2023 pages 88-91 and the counts moved: Food Service Licensing and Inspections 44 (was 39), Recreational Permitting and Inspections 8 (was 54), Housing & Nuisance Investigation 17 (unchanged). Title 5 counts are again inside sentences: 32 soil-test applications, 115 tests witnessed, 41 applications, 53 plans, 45 permits (19 new / 26 replacement), 153 construction inspections, 75 Title 5 reports.

rows.name: Fire department calls for service by category
rows.printed_heading: (none — introduced by 'In 2024, your Fire Department responded to 2083 calls for service, broken down as follows:')
rows.what_it_is: The year's fire and EMS call volume split four ways.
rows.columns: (category) | (count)
rows.layout: bulleted list rather than FY2023's two-column pairs
rows.printed_total: 2083 calls for service (stated in the introducing sentence)
rows.notes: Fires, Alarms & Hazardous Conditions 447; Emergency Medical 1193; Inspections 414; Other 29. These sum to 2,083 and the printed total TIES — unlike FY2023, whose four categories summed 100 short of its stated 2,033. Note Emergency Medical is 1193 in both years, exactly.

rows.name: Fire department roster
rows.printed_heading: FIRE DEPARTMENT / Roster of the Lunenburg Fire Department- 2024
rows.what_it_is: Every member of the fire department by name, rank and certification, grouped by shift and by career vs call.
rows.columns: A Shift | B Shift | C Shift
rows.layout: three shift columns under 'Career Firefighters', then a 'Call Firefighters' block
rows.notes: Same shape as FY2023 page 94 but OCR'd this year rather than laid out, so slightly worse. Rank and certification are inside the name string.

rows.name: Police department personnel roster
rows.printed_heading: (under the department letterhead 'POLICE DEPARTMENT ... Interim Chief Jeffrey Thibodeau')
rows.what_it_is: Sworn and civilian staff by assignment and shift.
rows.columns: (name with rank)
rows.layout: centred lists grouped by Administration / Day Shift / Evening Shift / Overnight / civilian
rows.notes: OCR quality poor across the whole police insert (79-85), as in FY2023. The department is led by an Interim Chief this year; Chief Thomas Gammel retired.

rows.name: Police department activity statistics
rows.printed_heading: Activity (under '2024 Statistical Information:')
rows.what_it_is: Calendar-year 2024 counts of police activity: calls, arrests, accidents, stops, citations, domestic violence, animal control, mental health, firearms licensing.
rows.columns: Activity | (count)
rows.layout: two-column list beginning at the foot of page 82 and continuing across page 83
rows.notes: Calls for Service 22,880 (was 23,040); Arrests Total 315; Motor Vehicle Stops 3,031; Citations Warnings 1836 (a large jump from 852); Firearms Licensing 306. Row labels differ slightly from FY2023 — 'Restraining Orders (RO)' replaces the unlabelled row FY2023 left blank, 'Mental Health Related Incidents' replaces 'Mental Health', 'Civil Citations (fines)' replaces 'Citations Civil (fines)'. Narrative adds 1,717 written reports (FY2023: 1,355), six use-of-force incidents, one pursuit.

rows.name: Regional dispatch 911 call volumes, five years
rows.printed_heading: 911 Calls:
rows.what_it_is: Nashoba Valley Regional Dispatch District call volumes by line type and disposition.
rows.grain: one line type x one disposition x one year
rows.layout: grouped table with a merged row-label column (911 / 10-Dig Emerg / 911 Admin)
rows.notes: THIS IS THE SAME TABLE AS FY2023 PAGE 103, CELL FOR CELL — it still ends at 2023 and contains no 2024 column. The FY2024 report reprints last year's dispatch figures unchanged, and the narrative under it still reads 'In 2023, NVRDD handled over 76,982 phone calls'. FY2023's companion table of monthly business/non-emergency calls was dropped.

rows.name: Regional dispatch calls by member town
rows.printed_heading: Police Related Calls:
rows.what_it_is: Police-related dispatch call counts by member community.
rows.layout: ten-row table
rows.notes: Also reprinted unchanged from FY2023 page 104 and still ending at 2023. The FY2024 OCR is slightly better and fills two cells FY2023's lost (Bolton 2020 = 6,917; Boxborough 2019/2020 = 0). Lunenburg 2023 = 14,385 in both.

rows.name: School staff rosters, by building
rows.printed_heading: LUNENBURG PRIMARY SCHOOL STAFF ROSTER (p104-105); Turkey Hill Elementary School Staff Roster (p107, and an unheaded second roster on p108); (middle school roster is unheaded, p110-111); (high school roster is unheaded, p114-115)
rows.what_it_is: Named staff at each school grouped by grade level, department or role, most with a room number or team colour.
rows.columns: (name) | (title / room / team)
rows.layout: two- to four-up column blocks per building
rows.notes: EIGHT pages of rosters. PAGES 107 AND 108 ARE TWO DIFFERENT TURKEY HILL ROSTERS PRINTED BACK TO BACK with the same section headings and different people in every leadership role — p107 has Norman Yvon as Principal, Bethann Cormier Assistant Principal, Elizabeth Schatia Nurse; p108 has Heidi Champagne, John Palumbo and Meghan Marrone. They appear to be two different school years and the report does not say which is which. The primary and Turkey Hill rosters carry room numbers; the elementary one also carries team colours (Blue/White/Red).

rows.name: Middle school MCAS results vs state
rows.printed_heading: Spring MCAS Score
rows.what_it_is: Percentage of Lunenburg Middle School students meeting or exceeding expectations by grade and subject, against the state.
rows.columns: (grade and subject) | % Meeting or Exceeding | % State Expectations
rows.layout: seven-row table in the middle of the page
rows.notes: THE HEADING LOST ITS YEAR — FY2023's read '2023 Spring MCAS Score', this one reads only 'Spring MCAS Score'. Worse, the explanatory paragraph directly beneath says '2022 Spring MCAS testing at LMS' and 'We look forward to what 2023 scores will indicate', which is text carried over from an older report. The figures differ from FY2023's table, so they are not the same data, but nothing on the page reliably states which year they are. Second column header also changed, from '% State Meeting or Exceeding' to '% State Expectations'.

rows.name: High school MCAS results vs state
rows.printed_heading: MCAS RESULTS / Lunenburg High School - Spring 2024 MCAS Results (Grade 10)
rows.what_it_is: Grade 10 MCAS meeting/exceeding percentages against the state average.
rows.columns: Subject Test | Exceeding Expectations / Meeting Expectations | State Average (EE/ME)
rows.layout: three-row table mid-page
rows.notes: ELA 68% vs 57%, Math 62% vs 48%, Science 64% vs 49%. The column header is complete here ('Exceeding Expectations / Meeting Expectations') where FY2023's was truncated. Note the surrounding prose repeats FY2023's claim of '30 students ... received the John and Abigail Adams Scholarship' word for word.

rows.name: Special education enrolment and DESE indicators
rows.printed_heading: SPECIAL SERVICES DEPARTMENT / Town Report – FY24 (data taken from 2023-2024 school year)
rows.what_it_is: Narrative that carries the district's special education counts and each DESE indicator with the state target, the Lunenburg rate and the state rate.
rows.grain: one DESE indicator (or one enrolment count)
rows.columns: Indicator n – (name) | state target | Lunenburg rate | state rate | (prior year in parentheses)
rows.layout: running prose, one paragraph per indicator; no ruled table
rows.notes: CONTAINS THE OUT-OF-DISTRICT PLACEMENT COUNTS, which are almost never published: 'the total number of students receiving services outside the district was 8 (last year was 7). Of the 8 students, 4 are placed in Collaborative Placements, 3 are in Day Placements and 1 are in Residential Placements.' Also 242 students with disabilities (228 last year), 15.5% of 1,566 total students (14.6% last year), state average 20.2%; 119 students on 504 plans (155 last year); ACE programme 7 students. Every figure is given with its prior-year value in parentheses, so the page is effectively a two-year table written as sentences. FY2023's equivalent section (pages 121-123) did not give the placement split.

rows.name: Monty Tech member towns
rows.printed_heading: OUR SCHOOL COMMUNITY
rows.what_it_is: The eighteen member towns, plus a gender pie and the year's enrolment.

rows.name: Town meeting article record with vote tallies

rows.notes: The header year is CORRECT this year ('2024 TOWN MEETING EXCERPTS' above the May 2024 meeting) where FY2023 printed '2022' above its May 2023 meeting. The vote format also changed and improved: FY2023 printed '(99 YES, 4 NO)'; FY2024 prints '(Yes-256, No-114, Abstain-2, Total-382)', so abstentions and the total voting are now recorded. Key budget articles: Article 7 raises $43,290,567.48 plus named transfers for an FY2025 total of $44,024,349.19; ARTICLE 8 raises $948,136 to supplement the school budget CONTINGENT ON A PROPOSITION 2½ BALLOT QUESTION, passed at town meeting Yes-256/No-114 — and the ballot question then FAILED at the election (see the election tally, Question 1 Override). Pages 148-171 are mostly the full text of two large bylaw amendments (Battery Energy Storage Systems, and a complete replacement of the Water Supply Protection District bylaw). Article 2 this year explicitly says the revolving fund limits are 'as printed in the Annual Town Meeting warrant' rather than reproducing them — FY2023 promised a table and printed nothing.
